fluff.overview: Clan Snow Raven became the first Clan to develop an OmniFighter when its technicians introduced the Issedone in 2871, drawing directly on the semi-modular Spad light fighter that the Clan had inherited from its Star League-era stores. Just as Clan Coyote had based the first OmniMech on the modular Mercury II, the Ravens leveraged the Spad's maintenance-friendly design to create their new fighter quickly. The result pleased the Clan's technicians, though the Issedone was never as effective as the Issus and Chaeronea fighters already in frontline service. Despite these limitations, it performed yeoman work for the next century before gradually fading into obsolescence. In a surprising development, Clan Sea Fox later reintroduced the Issedone and has found steady sales in tertiary markets like the Periphery, a sign of how solid the basic package remains.
fluff.capabilities:
The Issedone's saving grace is its nine tons of available pod space, generous for a thirty-ton airframe. The base chassis retains the F-50/C frame and GM 150 fusion engine of its Spad ancestor, providing safe thrust of 7 and a maximum of 11. Ten single heat sinks handle baseline thermal load, though most configurations add pod-mounted sinks to compensate for energy-heavy loadouts. Seven and a half tons of Carbondale III armor afford reasonable protection, but a reckless pilot can quickly find it insufficient against sustained fire.

The Issedone debuted seventeen years after the first OmniMech and faced the same technical limitations that plagued early land-air machines and first-generation aerospace OmniPods. Nine tons of Clan-technology equipment can make any light airframe dangerous, and the fighter uses that capacity effectively. Like the Spad before it, the Issedone is valued by technicians for its ruggedness and ease of servicing. Its CMDSTAT 500-A communications system and Scope Paint v2.41 targeting suite represent incremental upgrades over the Spad's original electronics, maintaining the design philosophy of reliability over sophistication.
fluff.deployment: A dedicated missile platform, the B configuration carries an LRM-10 in each wing with two tons of CASE-protected ammunition for twenty-four volleys. Two ER medium lasers provide backup firepower, with one mounted in the nose and one covering the rear arc to discourage pursuit.
fluff.history:
The Issedone entered service with Clan Snow Raven during the early Golden Century, born from a deliberate effort to apply OmniMech technology to aerospace platforms. Starting from a single Point, Issedones gradually spread through the Raven touman as the Clan refined its OmniFighter doctrine. The design never displaced the Issus or Chaeronea in frontline roles, but it carved out a useful niche in garrison and second-line formations where its flexibility and low maintenance requirements were prized over raw performance.

The Issedone found its defining moment during the Steel Viper conflict on Hellgate in the late twenty-ninth century. When Clan Steel Viper captured the Ravens' agro-domes on the planet in 2897, the Snow Ravens were forced to choose between importing civilian supplies and weapons to fight off continued Viper incursions. In these deprived conditions, the Issedone thrived. Starting from a single Point, the fighters soon became the preferred choice for Raven pilots on Hellgate, and ultimately a full Trinary was stationed there. As more capable fighters were grounded for lack of spare parts, Issedones were sent time and again to blunt Viper assaults using whatever weapons were available. Over eighteen months, the Vipers escalated from fielding vintage SLDF fighters to modern Clan craft, but none could overcome the combination of the hostile environment and the Issedone's relentless combat tempo. When the Ravens finally pulled out of Hellgate in 2899, the Vipers could muster only a pair of Spads to harass the retreating DropShips and their Issedone escorts.

One Snow Raven officer earned particular distinction during the Hellgate campaign. Arriving in 2898, he demanded increasingly fast turnaround times from his technicians and launched almost-daily dawn raids on Steel Viper airfields. The first Viper attempt to trap him nearly succeeded, but the second resulted in a Binary of Viper fighters being drawn into a Raven counter-trap that left the Vipers outnumbered for the following three months. He went on to a distinguished career, eventually rising to command a Snow Raven capital vessel.

Another notable Issedone pilot commanded a Leopard CV of mercenaries providing technical assistance to Lyran defenders against Clan Jade Falcon. Avoiding direct engagements, he used his forces as spotters and harassers behind enemy lines. His most significant success came when he penetrated airspace over a Jade Falcon spaceport with his Issedone C, calling down guided missile strikes from the rest of his squadron that destroyed two DropShips.

The original Crest Foundries production line on Lum ceased operations at some point, and MUPL records show no active production eras for that facility. Clan Sea Fox later established or acquired production capability at DS Aero Assembly Site Rho on Twycross, an underground facility built to withstand the planet's frequent tornadoes. This line became active during the Late Republic era and continues into the ilClan period under the Alyina Mercantile League. Sea Fox introduced the C and D configurations specifically for export, incorporating Inner Sphere vendor components like chaff pods and ProtoMech autocannons to appeal to a broader customer base.
